lessons.title: Listen and speak: a telephone call
lessons.objective: Hold a short telephone conversation politely: greet, say who is speaking, ask and answer, say goodbye.
lessons.course:
On the telephone, we greet, we say who we are, we speak clearly and we say goodbye.
Hello! This is Manka. May I speak to Auntie, please? … Thank you. Goodbye!

support.title: Play with the adult
support.text:
Hello! This is Manka.
How are you?
I am fine, thank you.
Goodbye!

lessons.model: The adult takes a toy phone: “Hello! This is Mama Ngum. How are you, Bih?” The child answers: “I am fine, thank you.”
lessons.guided: Play a call with two toy phones: greet, give your name, ask how the other person is, say goodbye.
lessons.exercise: Someone calls you. What do you say first?
lessons.remediation: Practise only the start (Hello! This is …) and the end (Goodbye!).
lessons.transfer: With an adult, call a member of the family and greet them politely.
lessons.materials: Two toy phones or two cups and a string.

practice.prompt: Put the telephone call in order.
practice.answer: Hello! This is Manka. How are you? I am fine, thank you. Goodbye!
practice.explanation: We greet first and say goodbye at the end.

practice.prompt: Listen and answer like in a call.
practice.explanation: Answer politely.

practice.prompt: How do we end a call?
practice.explanation: We say goodbye at the end of a call.

lessons.title: Read a short message silently
lessons.objective: Read a short message silently and answer questions about it.
lessons.course:
A message gives news to someone. It says who writes, to whom, and what the news is.
We read it silently, with our eyes, then we answer questions.

support.title: Read silently
support.text:
Dear Grandma,
We have a new baby goat. It is white and small.
Come and see it on Sunday.
Love, Ayuk

lessons.model: The adult reads a message silently, then says: “Ayuk writes to Grandma. The news is about a baby goat.”
lessons.guided: Read the message silently. Then find: Who writes? To whom? What is the news? When should Grandma come?
lessons.remediation: Read the message aloud together first, then answer.
lessons.transfer: Read a short message on a card or a phone with an adult.
lessons.materials: The message written on a card.

practice.prompt: What colour is the baby goat?
practice.explanation: The message says: It is white and small.

practice.prompt: When should Grandma come?
practice.explanation: The message says: Come and see it on Sunday.

practice.prompt: Match the question with its answer.
practice.explanation: All the answers are in the message.

lessons.title: Write a short message
lessons.objective: Write a message of one or two short sentences with one’s name.
lessons.course:
A message has three parts: to whom (Dear Papa,), the news in one or two short sentences, and our name at the end.
Each sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

support.title: Copy with the adult
support.text:
Dear Papa,
I can read. I love you.
Bih

lessons.model: The adult writes a short card: “Dear Mama, I am at school. See you soon. Neba”.
lessons.guided: Choose a person. Say your news aloud, then write it in one sentence. Sign with your name.
lessons.exercise: Write a message to a friend: say “Come and play.” and sign your name.
lessons.answer: For example: Dear Tabi, Come and play. Ayuk
lessons.remediation: Copy the model message and change only the name of the person.
lessons.transfer: Write a small card for someone in your family.

practice.prompt: Write your message on the lines.
practice.answer: A message with a greeting, a short sentence and the name.
practice.explanation: Start with Dear …, end with your name.

practice.prompt: Put the parts of the message in order.
practice.answer: Dear Mama, / I am at school. / Neba
practice.explanation: Greeting first, name last.

practice.prompt: Where do we write our name in a message?
practice.explanation: We sign at the end.

lessons.title: And, but, and the future with will
lessons.objective: Link words and sentences with and or but, and talk about tomorrow with will.
lessons.course:
And joins two things: Bih and Tabi. I read and I write.
But shows a difference: I can read, but I cannot drive.
For tomorrow, we use will + verb: Tomorrow I will call Grandma.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
Bih and Tabi
I can sing, but I cannot fly.
Tomorrow I will write.

lessons.model: The adult says: “I have a phone and a radio. The radio is old, but it works. Tomorrow I will call Papa.”
lessons.guided: Join two picture cards with and. Then say something you will do tomorrow with will.
lessons.exercise: Join with and: Manka sings. Manka dances.
lessons.remediation: Practise with and only, using two objects.
lessons.transfer: Tell an adult two things you will do tomorrow.

practice.prompt: Complete with and or but.
practice.text: I have a pen [[and]] a book. The phone is small [[but]] it is loud.
practice.explanation: And adds; but shows a difference.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is about tomorrow?
practice.explanation: Will + verb tells about the future.

practice.prompt: Complete: Tomorrow I ___ write a letter.
accept: Tomorrow I will write a letter
practice.explanation: will + write: future.

lessons.title: A timetable: what happens when
lessons.objective: Read a simple daily timetable and respect a schedule.
lessons.course:
A timetable tells what happens and when. At school: Monday, English; Tuesday, Mathematics… At home: morning, wash; afternoon, homework; night, sleep.
We follow the timetable to be on time.
lessons.model: The adult shows a family timetable for the radio programme: “On Saturday morning we listen to the children’s programme.”
lessons.guided: Make a timetable of your day with pictures: morning, afternoon, night. Read it aloud.
lessons.exercise: In your timetable, when do you do your homework?
lessons.remediation: Use three pictures only, one for each period.
lessons.transfer: Put your timetable on the wall at home and follow it.
lessons.materials: Paper, pictures or drawings of activities.

practice.prompt: Put Neba’s Saturday in order.
practice.explanation: Follow the periods of the day.

practice.prompt: Why do we follow a timetable?
practice.explanation: A timetable helps us to do things at the right time.

practice.prompt: How many days of school are there in a week?
practice.explanation: Monday to Friday: 5 days.

lessons.title: Shopping problems up to 100 francs
lessons.objective: Pay, add prices and give change with amounts up to 100 francs.
lessons.course:
To know how much to pay, we add the prices. A pen costs 50 francs, an eraser 25 francs: 50 + 25 = 75 francs.
To know the change, we take away: we pay 100 francs for 75 francs, the change is 25 francs.
lessons.model: The adult buys a phone card for 100 francs with two coins of 50 francs: “50 and 50 make 100. No change.”
lessons.guided: Play shop with price labels and coins. Add two prices, pay, and count the change.
lessons.exercise: A notebook costs 60 francs. You pay 100 francs. What is the change?
lessons.remediation: Use prices that are tens (20, 30, 50) first.
lessons.transfer: With an adult, check the change after buying bread.

practice.prompt: A pencil costs 25 francs and a ruler costs 50 francs. Total in francs?
You pay 100 francs for something that costs 90 francs. Change in francs?
Which coins make 75 francs?

lessons.title: A bar graph of messages
lessons.objective: Represent data with a simple bar graph and answer questions about it.
lessons.course:
A bar graph uses bars to show how many. The taller the bar, the more there are.
We count the squares in each bar to read the number.
lessons.model: The adult counts the messages received by the family in one week: Monday 2, Tuesday 4, Wednesday 1. Then colours one square per message.
lessons.guided: Collect a small set of data (letters, calls or visitors in a week). Colour one square for each and compare the bars.
lessons.exercise: Monday: 2 squares, Tuesday: 4 squares, Wednesday: 1 square. Which day had the most messages?
lessons.remediation: Build each bar with real blocks before colouring squares.
lessons.transfer: Make a bar graph of the weather for one week (sun, rain).

practice.prompt: How many messages on Tuesday?
practice.explanation: The Tuesday bar has 4 squares.

practice.prompt: Which day had the fewest messages?
practice.explanation: The Wednesday bar is the shortest.

practice.prompt: How many messages in all on the three days?

lessons.title: Numbers to 100 in words: review
lessons.objective: Read and write numbers up to 100 in figures and in words, and use them in sentences.
lessons.course:
We write numbers in words with the tens and the units: 46 → forty-six; 99 → ninety-nine.
A hyphen joins the tens and the units: twenty-one, eighty-five.
lessons.model: The adult writes a telephone message: “Call me at 5 o’clock. My number ends with 48: forty-eight.”
lessons.guided: Write numbers in words on cards, then match them with figure cards.
lessons.remediation: Write the tens in words first (fifty), then add the units.
lessons.transfer: Read the numbers of a calendar or a telephone aloud in English.
lessons.materials: Number cards in figures and in words.

practice.prompt: Write in figures: eighty-two.
practice.explanation: Eighty is 80, two is 2: 82.

practice.prompt: Match each number with its words.
practice.explanation: Read the tens, then the units.

practice.prompt: Complete in words.
practice.explanation: Tens word, hyphen, units word.

lessons.title: Electrical devices and their dangers
lessons.objective: Identify some electrical devices and the dangers of using them wrongly; ask an adult for help.
lessons.course:
Electrical devices work with electricity: the radio, the television, the phone charger, the fridge, the bulb.
Electricity can hurt us. We never touch a socket, a broken wire or a device with wet hands. We ask an adult to plug or unplug a device.
lessons.model: Enow wants to charge the phone. He calls his father, who plugs the charger into the socket.
lessons.guided: Look at pictures of devices. Sort them: works with electricity or not. Then say the safety rules together.
lessons.exercise: Who should plug a device into the socket?
lessons.remediation: Use two pictures: a radio (electricity) and a book (no electricity).
lessons.transfer: Show an adult the sockets in your house and say the safety rule.
lessons.materials: Pictures of electrical devices and of things without electricity.

practice.prompt: Which one works with electricity?
practice.explanation: A television needs electricity to work.

practice.prompt: Is it safe to touch a socket with wet hands? Answer yes or no.
practice.explanation: Water and electricity together are very dangerous.

practice.prompt: Match each device with what it does.
practice.answer: radio: sound; bulb: light; fridge: cold.
practice.explanation: Electrical devices help us in many ways.

lessons.title: J’écris une petite phrase
lessons.objective: Tenir correctement le crayon, recopier des mots et remettre des mots dans l’ordre pour faire une phrase avec une majuscule et un point.
lessons.course:
Une phrase commence par une majuscule et finit par un point.
« papa / lit / Le / journal » devient : « Le papa lit le journal. »
On tient le crayon entre le pouce et l’index, posé sur le majeur.
lessons.model: L’adulte écrit « Maman appelle papa. » et montre : « M majuscule au début, un point à la fin. »
lessons.guided: Avec des étiquettes, remets les mots dans l’ordre, lis la phrase, puis recopie-la.
lessons.remediation: Recopie d’abord un seul mot, puis une phrase de deux mots.
lessons.transfer: Écris « Bonjour maman » sur une carte.

practice.prompt: Remets les mots dans l’ordre.
practice.explanation: La majuscule est au début, le point à la fin.

practice.prompt: Recopie la phrase : Je lis.
practice.explanation: J majuscule, point à la fin.

practice.prompt: Qu’est-ce qu’on met à la fin d’une phrase ?
practice.explanation: Une phrase finit par un point.

lessons.title: The flag, the anthem and the motto of Cameroon
lessons.objective: Identify the national emblems of Cameroon and show respect during the anthem and the hoisting of the flag.
lessons.course:
Cameroon has national emblems. The flag has three vertical colours: green, red and yellow, with a yellow star in the middle of the red. The motto is “Peace – Work – Fatherland”. The national anthem is sung on important days and at school.
When the flag is hoisted or the anthem is sung, we stand still, we stop talking and we look at the flag.
lessons.model: On Monday morning, the pupils line up. The flag goes up. Everyone stands still and quiet while the anthem is sung.
lessons.guided: Colour the flag: green, red with a yellow star, yellow. Practise standing still and quiet during a song.
lessons.exercise: What are the three colours of the flag of Cameroon?
lessons.remediation: Colour the three bands one by one with the adult.
lessons.transfer: Show the flag to someone at home and say the motto.
lessons.materials: Coloured pencils, a drawing of the flag to colour.

practice.prompt: Put the colours of the flag in order, from left to right.
practice.explanation: The star is in the red band.

practice.prompt: What do we do when the anthem is sung?
practice.explanation: We show respect to the nation.

practice.prompt: Complete the motto.
practice.explanation: This is the motto of Cameroon.

lessons.title: A greeting card to send
lessons.objective: Produce a decoration item with materials from the environment: a greeting card.
lessons.course: We decorate to make things beautiful. A greeting card is a folded paper with a drawing and a short message. We can decorate it with seeds, small leaves, colours or paper flowers.
lessons.model: Ayuk folds a paper in two, draws a flower, sticks small seeds around it and writes: “Happy birthday, Mama.”
lessons.guided: Fold a paper in two. Decorate the front with materials. Ask the adult to help you write a short message inside.
lessons.exercise: What is inside a greeting card?
lessons.remediation: Decorate with colours only, then add one material.
lessons.transfer: Give your card to someone you love.
lessons.materials: Paper, coloured pencils, glue, seeds, small dry leaves.

practice.prompt: Put the steps in order.
practice.explanation: Follow the steps to make a card.

practice.prompt: Which material can decorate a card?
practice.explanation: Seeds can be glued on paper.

practice.prompt: Draw the front of your card.
practice.explanation: Use bright colours.

lessons.title: Drums and other instruments that speak
lessons.objective: Identify traditional musical instruments and say how they were used to send messages.
lessons.course:
Cameroon has many traditional instruments: the drum, the talking drum, the balafon (a wooden xylophone), the rattle, the flute.
Long ago, some drums sent messages from village to village: a meeting, a birth, danger.
lessons.model: The adult beats a tin like a drum: two slow beats, three fast beats: “This could call the village to a meeting.”
lessons.guided: Look at pictures of instruments. Make a rattle with a bottle and seeds. Play a beat to send a “message” to the others.
lessons.exercise: Which instrument was used to send messages between villages?
lessons.remediation: Name two instruments with pictures: the drum and the rattle.
lessons.transfer: Ask an elder about an instrument played in your village.
lessons.materials: Pictures of instruments, a plastic bottle, seeds, a tin.

practice.prompt: Match each instrument with how we play it.
practice.answer: drum: beat; rattle: shake; flute: blow.
practice.explanation: Instruments are played in different ways.

practice.prompt: What is a balafon made of?
practice.explanation: The balafon has wooden keys.

practice.prompt: Name one traditional instrument.
practice.answer: For example: the drum, the balafon, the rattle.
practice.explanation: Cameroon has many traditional instruments.

lessons.title: Jumping the rope
lessons.objective: Jump over a turning rope and count the jumps.
lessons.course:
Two children turn a long rope. The jumper waits, enters when the rope goes up, jumps with two feet together each time the rope touches the ground, and counts.
We jump on soft ground and land on the front of the feet.
lessons.model: Manka enters and jumps: “One, two, three, four…” Her friends count with her.
lessons.guided: Turn the rope with a friend and take turns to jump. Count the jumps aloud.
lessons.exercise: When do we enter to jump the rope?
lessons.remediation: Jump over a rope lying still on the ground first, then a rope moving slowly.
lessons.transfer: Play rope jumping with friends and count your best score.

practice.prompt: Tabi jumps 7 times, then 5 times. How many jumps in all?
How do we land?
choices: on the front of the feet
practice.answer: on the front of the feet
practice.explanation: Landing softly protects the legs.

practice.prompt: How many children turn the long rope?
practice.explanation: One at each end.

lessons.title: A tale from the elders
lessons.objective: Listen to a short tale or song from the family, retell it and name the members of the nuclear family in the home language.
lessons.course:
Elders keep stories, tales, songs and proverbs. They tell them in the evening, often in the family language. Tales teach lessons: be kind, be patient, do not be greedy.
The nuclear family is father, mother and children. We learn to name them in our language.
lessons.model: In the evening, Grandmother tells a short tale about the tortoise in her language. Then Enow retells it in English.
lessons.guided: Ask an elder to tell you a short tale or a song in the family language. Retell it in a few sentences. Learn the words for father, mother, brother and sister.
lessons.exercise: Who keeps the tales of the family?
lessons.remediation: Listen to a very short tale twice before retelling it.
lessons.transfer: Record a family word or a short song in Klassia’s “Home language” page, with an adult.

practice.prompt: Retell the tale you heard in three sentences.
practice.answer: The tale retold in three sentences.
practice.explanation: Say the beginning, the middle and the end.

practice.prompt: Match each member of the family with the English word.
pairs: the man who is your parent
the woman who is your parent
a boy with the same parents
practice.explanation: These are members of the nuclear family.

practice.prompt: What do tales teach us?
practice.explanation: Tales teach kindness, patience and wisdom.

lessons.title: A polite phone call and private messages
lessons.objective: Use a phone (pretend) to communicate at a distance politely and respect other people’s privacy.
lessons.course:
With a phone we can talk to people far away. We greet, say who we are, speak clearly and say goodbye.
Messages and photos on another person’s phone are private: we do not read them without permission.
lessons.model: Bih borrows her aunt’s phone to call her father. She does not open the aunt’s messages. She gives the phone back and says thank you.
lessons.guided: Play a call with a toy phone. Then discuss: may we look at the messages on someone else’s phone?
lessons.exercise: May we read the messages on someone else’s phone without permission?
lessons.remediation: Practise only greeting and goodbye on the phone.
lessons.transfer: Ask permission before using a phone at home.

practice.prompt: Put the call in order.
practice.answer: Hello! This is Bih. I am fine, thank you. Goodbye!
practice.explanation: Greet, say who you are, talk, say goodbye.

practice.prompt: What do we say when we give back a phone we borrowed?
practice.explanation: We thank the person.

practice.prompt: What does “private” mean?
practice.answer: It belongs to one person; others do not look without permission.
practice.explanation: We respect other people’s privacy.
